summary: Payment failures began at ~12:15Z on 2026-04-02 and are caused by the expiry of payment-service's client mTLS certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z). After expiry, all calls to bank-partner-api fail the TLS handshake with 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' and payments are queued as PENDING_RETRY. payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.5% and bank_api_error_rate rose to 100%, but the HTTP error_rate panel stayed flat (~0.2%) because no 5xx is returned — successfully hiding the incident from the dashboard. Resource metrics, traffic, deployments and the unrelated timeout config change were all ruled out. This matches historical incident HIST-106 (credential_expiry, no renewal automation). Remediation: renew/rotate the client certificate and add expiry-aware rotation automation.

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service client mTLS certificate expired, breaking bank-partner-api calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal used by payment-service to authenticate to bank-partner-api expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. All outbound bank calls then failed the mTLS handshake, so transfers were marked PENDING_RETRY and payment_success_rate fell to ~2.5% while bank_api_error_rate hit 100%. The HTTP error_rate panel stayed green because payment-service queues retries instead of returning 5xx. Fault originates in payment-service credential management.

causal_chain.claim: At 12:15 the cert expired; bank-partner-api mTLS handshakes were rejected with alert 45
Failed bank calls -> payments marked PENDING_RETRY (no HTTP 5xx)
payment_success_rate collapsed to ~2.5% and bank_api_error_rate hit 100%, while error_rate stayed ~0.2%

assumptions: No cert renewal occurred between the 11:50 warning and expiry
bank-partner-api correctly rejects an expired client cert (alert 45 is standard TLS expired-certificate alert)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank partner API-side outage (dependency_failure)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: bank-partner-api itself was failing, causing payment failures. Contradicted because logs explicitly report OUR client cert expired (alert 45, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) — the rejection is triggered by our expired credential, and onset exactly matches our cert's notAfter.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Error message is a TLS expired-certificate alert naming our own client cert with notAfter equal to the onset; not a partner 5xx. HIST-105 (partner 5xx) doesn't fit the message.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / capacity saturation on payment-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: CPU, memory, DB connection pool or traffic overload caused the failures. Contradicted: cpu flat ~30%, db_pool_in_use flat ~8, restarts 0, request_rate steady ~100 req/s, and latency DECREASED (fast handshake failures, not saturation).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: All saturation indicators flat or improving; latency fell rather than rising.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000) caused the fault
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 11:20 timeout config change broke payments. Contradicted: it predates onset by 55 minutes, changes only a timeout (not TLS trust/renewal), and onset aligns exactly with cert notAfter=12:15. Also a timeout increase could not produce an 'expired certificate' alert.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing mismatch (55 min gap) and semantically unrelated to mTLS certificate errors.

facts.statement: payment-service HTTP error_rate stayed flat (~0.2-0.32%) through the incident.
payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.5% starting at 12:10-12:20Z.
cert-watcher warned the payments-client certificate would expire at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z.
bank-partner-api calls failed with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' from 12:16Z.
Failed payments were marked PENDING_RETRY due to rejected mTLS handshake.
Latency decreased at onset (fast handshake failures, not timeouts).
CPU, DB pool and restarts were flat; no resource exhaustion.
No payment-service deployment; only an unrelated settlement-service deploy at 10:30Z.
Only config change was bank.api.timeout_ms at 11:20Z, unrelated to TLS and 55 min before onset.
Request rate was steady ~100 req/s; no traffic surge.
HIST-106 was a prior credential_expiry incident (client cert expired, no renewal automation).

assumptions: cert-watcher's notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z is authoritative for the client cert's expiry.
TLS alert 45 denotes certificate_expired and is emitted because our client cert is expired, not the partner's.
No certificate rotation occurred between the 11:50 warning and expiry.

timeline.event: payment-service config change bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 — unrelated to TLS
cert-watcher warns payments-client certificate expires in 25 min (notAfter 12:15Z)
payment_success_rate begins to fall; bank_api_error_rate begins to rise (partial bucket)
client certificate expires; mTLS handshakes to bank-partner-api rejected
first 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' errors from bank-partner-api calls
support lead reports ~40 failed-transfer tickets; error-rate panel still green

recommended_actions.action: Renew and install a valid client certificate for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal and restart/reload payment-service TLS config
recommended_actions.rationale: The expired cert (notAfter 12:15Z) is the direct cause of all bank-partner-api handshake failures.

recommended_actions.action: Reprocess/retry the payments queued as PENDING_RETRY and verify success_rate recovers to ~99%
recommended_actions.rationale: Fund transfers are stuck; customers reported ~40 failures.

recommended_actions.action: Fix alerting: add a firing alarm on payment_success_rate and bank_api_error_rate (not just HTTP error_rate), since PENDING_RETRY masks failures from the 5xx panel
recommended_actions.rationale: The green error_rate dashboard hid a full payment outage.

recommended_actions.action: Implement automated certificate rotation with expiry alerting at multiple lead times satisfying the cert-watcher warning
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-106 was the same credential_expiry pattern; recurrence shows the renewal gap was never fixed.

data_gaps: bank-partner-api has no telemetry (has_telemetry:false), so we cannot independently confirm the partner side behaved normally; H2 (partner outage) is rejected on the strength of our own error messages rather than partner-side evidence.

No direct metric for certificate validity/expiry time-series; the expiry is confirmed only via the cert-watcher warning log and the error text (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z), not an observable metric.
Root-cause of why the cert was not renewed (owner/process failure) is not visible in the available data — no cert-management or secret-store telemetry was queried.

payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.5% starting at the 12:10-12:20 bucket and stayed there.
bank_api_error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to 100% at the 12:10-12:20 bucket and remained 100%.

findings.statement: Failed payments are marked 'PENDING_RETRY' due to rejected mTLS handshake (140 occurrences), explaining why no HTTP 5xx are emitted.

refs.quote: payment <n> marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected

findings.statement: payment-service latency_p99_ms DECREASED at onset (from ~320ms to ~140ms), consistent with requests failing fast at the mTLS handshake rather than timing out.
payment-service cpu_pct stayed flat at ~30% and db_pool_in_use flat at ~8 connections; restarts remained 0 throughout.
No deployment to payment-service in the window (count 0); the only deployment was settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30Z (a CSV exporter), unrelated to payment TLS.
The only payment-service config change was bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20:00Z — 55 minutes before the 12:15 onset and unrelated to TLS.
payment-service request_rate stayed steady at ~100 req/s through the incident — traffic did not surge (rules out capacity saturation).
api-gateway logged no WARN/ERROR entries in the window (0 matches), so the failure is not surfacing as gateway errors.
Prior HIST-106 (settlement mTLS certificate expired, 2025-06-30) had the same category 'credential_expiry' with root cause 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation'.
